### What operating system are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

6.3.11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

22

### Expected Behavior

- Run `electron-fiddle --enable-features=UseOzonePlatform --ozone-platform=wayland`.
- Electron fiddle editor shows up.

### Actual Behavior

Electron fiddle crashed after creating the main window.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

I'm using Sway as the compositor.

[core.zip](https://github.com/electron/electron/files/12308385/core.zip)

OS: Arch Linux x86_64
 Kernel: 6.5.3-arch1-1
 Compositor: Sway

After updating to v1.82.0-1, my instance always crashes when trying to open VSC in Wayland mode:
```
Warning: 'enable-features' is not in the list of known options, but still passed to Electron/Chromium.
Warning: 'ozone-platform' is not in the list of known options, but still passed to Electron/Chromium.
```
Before this update, VSC ran just fine in native Wayland with HiDPI screens and also without these warnings.

My config flags look like this (`code-flags.conf`):
```
--enable-features=UseOzonePlatform
--ozone-platform=wayland
```

Removing this config allows the program to start up normally, but not in native Wayland mode. The font and all visuals are very blurry as I'm on 3200x1800 monitor. Is there any other workaround for this or do I just need to wait until this is resolved? I don't think that downgrading is good way to solve this either for me.

> This crash is the upstream issue of [microsoft/vscode#184124](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/184124). If we look at the data there, >20 users have reported this electron crash. This implies possibly there are hundreds of unreported instances.

For visibility:  On the downstream & other issues (microsoft/vscode#184124, electron/electron#37531) you can find stacktraces with debug symbols.  All signs seem to point towards a [race condition][1] type of issue during startup & menu build.

Some example stacktraces  (thanks to `coredumpctl` + `gdb`):

- [Build Views with Layers][2]
  - VSCode Log error: `ERROR:elf_dynamic_array_reader.h(64)] tag not found`
  - Stacktrace Crashed in: `#0  0x0000562d9cd48f77 _ZN5views12_GLOBAL__N_120BuildViewsWithLayersEPNS_4ViewEPSt6vectorIS2_SaIS2_EE (electron + 0x8da0f77)`
  - Function: `views::(anonymous namespace)::BuildViewsWithLayers(views::View*, std::vector<views::View*, std::allocator<views::View*> >*) ()`
- [Update Child Layer Bounds][3]
  - VSCode Log error: `ERROR:elf_dynamic_array_reader.h(64)] tag not found`
  - Stacktrace Crashed in: `#0  0x000055c8c9767d69 _ZN5views4View22UpdateChildLayerBoundsERKNS0_15LayerOffsetDataE (electron + 0x8d83d69)`
  - Function: `views::View::UpdateChildLayerBounds(views::View::LayerOffsetData const&) ()`

Reproduction case is pretty easy:  Simply install & try to start VSCode on ArchLinux + Wayland desktop environment (e.g. Sway), Manjaro Sway edition, or other Arch-based distros with Wayland-based desktop environment (e.g. EndeavourOS, Garuda Linux, etc...).

I reproduced on [Manjaro Sway Edition][4]:

```sh
# For fresh OS install, best to use local repo mirrors...
sudo pacman-mirrors -f && sudo pacman -Syyu

# Install VSCode (a.k.a. "Code - OSS")
sudo pacman -Syu code

# Try to start VSCode under Wayland
#   + `"window.titleBarStyle": "native"
#   = Frequent Crash due to race condition during startup window & menu build
/usr/bin/code --ozone-platform-hint=wayland --enable-features=WaylandWindowDecorations --enable-features=WebRTCPipeWireCapturer --force-dark-mode  --verbose

# Crash + coredump visible via: coredumpctl list
```

**Note:** [Manjaro does not yet ship `debuginfod` debug symbols][5] for `code`, nor `electron25`, so these [must be built manually][2].  You may have better out-of-the-box support for `debuginfod` debug symbols on "vanilla" Arch Linux.  Although, first-time installation of ArchLinux in general requires a bit of *nix knowledge & time.  The crash should be easily reproducible on Wayland + Sway, and probably other similar desktop environments (e.g. Hyprland, River, Wayfire, etc...)

> Is there a chance this bug can be prioritized?

+1 to this!  Many appear to be affected.  Please & Thank You :<nick>:

> The font and all visuals are very blurry as I'm on 3200x1800 monitor. ### Off-topic: @participant3: This is most probably a separate issue and is not related to VSCode nor Electron.
Expand for possible solution

Check your monitor's native physical DPI & subpixel layout, then configure this in [`fontconfig`][1]. The values for `rgba` setting can be [found here under the "**Configuration File Format -> ``** section][2]. > [...SNIP...] > > unknown rgba 0 > rgb rgba 1 > bgr rgba 2 > vrgb rgba 3 > vbgr rgba 4 > none rgba 5 > > [...SNIP...] For example my monitor had BGR (blue-green-red) subpixel layout, and 36 DPI:

Expand for example fontconfig settings (~/.config/fontconfig/conf.d/19-DisplayProperties.conf)

`~/.config/fontconfig/conf.d/19-DisplayProperties.conf`: ``` 2 1 1.0 36.0 ```

Then afterwards rebuild fontconfig cache `fc-cache -frv`. Probably you should also restart Sway (or simply reboot for good measure), then check Sway's "`Scaling Factor`" is set to `1.0`, and that "`Subpixel hinting`" also matches your subpixel layout: `swaymsg -t get_outputs` If it doesn't match, then set them for your monitor (a.k.a. "Output" in Sway-terminology). For example:
Expand for example Sway output config ~/.config/sway/config.d/01-output-hdmi-subpixel-layout-scale.conf:

```hcl output "VIZIO, Inc M601d-A3/A3R 0x00000101" { subpixel bgr scale 1.0 } ```

> My config flags look like this (`code-flags.conf`): > > ``` > --enable-features=UseOzonePlatform > --ozone-platform=wayland > ``` If you're not starting `code` with these flags, then it will be using [XWayland][3] compatibility layer, and thus rendered through the Xorg display manager protocol -> Xwayland -> Wayland adapter code path. As such, some things may not work as well as a native Wayland application. You can verify which apps are running over XWayland by running: `xlsclients` (this program is available in `xorg-xlsclients` package on ArchLinux-based distros). > Is there any other workaround for this or do I just need to wait until this is resolved? A workaround for the crash race condition issue that seems to work for many people is to change the following setting in VScode's `settings.json`:
Expand for VSCode crash bug settings.json workaround

**Note:** The VSCode `settings.json` file may be located in an alternate location depending on whether you're using the OSS version of VSCode (a.k.a. VSCodium), or the official VScode from Microsoft. Usually located at: - VSCode Official or `code-features` version: `~/.config/Code/User/settings.json` - VSCode OSS or `code` w/o `code-features`: `~/.config/Code\ -\ OSS/User/settings.json` ``` # [... SNIP ...] "window.titleBarStyle": "custom", # [... SNIP ...] ``` This will usually result in _**less frequent**_ crashes during startup. Due to the nature of race conditions, you may want to retry starting `code` many times in succession to get it to succeed. Another thing to try is opening a pre-existing VSCode workspace, as this can affect startup timing & thus impact which thread wins the "race": `/usr/bin/code --ozone-platform-hint=wayland --enable-features=WaylandWindowDecorations --enable-features=WebRTCPipeWireCapturer --force-dark-mode --verbose ~/path/to/your/vscode/project.code-workspace`

**`code` on Arch Linux Note:**: ArchLinux-based distros use the VSCode OSS version, and the `code` package is by default setup to remove any Microsoft-specific telemetry, VSCode Extensions Marketplace (replaced by [OpenVSX][5]), and profile/settings Synchronization to Microsoft-controlled servers. This is due to an apparent licensing restriction from the non-100% OSS-friendly license which Microsoft has placed on their official VSCode release. _"I'm not a lawyer", so whether these licensing restrictions are real or just apparently assumed due to legalese interpretations is unknown to me._ Some features may be re-enabled by installing the [`code-features` package from the AUR][4]. After installing this package, it patches the `/usr/lib/code/product.json` file included in the OSS-`code` package to be more in-parity with Microsoft's official version. However, this package still does not replace OpenVSX with Microsoft's VSCode Extensions Marketplace because the `extensionsGallery` URLs in `product.json` are not changed.
[1]: https:///title/Font_configuration#top-page [2]: https://www.freedesktop.org/software/fontconfig/fontconfig-user.html#AEN191 [3]: https:///title/wayland#Xwayland [4]: https:///packages/code-features [5]: https://open-vsx.org/vscode/gallery

comments.body:
Some more data points potentially helpful for finding & fixing this crash bug:

I just tried running the same VSCode (`code` version `1.82.0-2` package on Manjaro) against the [`electron27-bin` package from the AUR][1] (version: `27.0.0beta.4-1`).  Even without the workaround (e.g. With setting: `"window.titleBarStyle": "native"`), so far I have been **unable to reproduce the crash against `electron27` beta**.

However, the following things are notable:

- Logs from `code --verbose` show many errors relating to incompatible version of `npm`
  - This is probably to be expected given that I did not upgrade `npm` on this system since testing the older `electron22` & `electron25` + VSCode stacks.
  - `code --verbose` logs here: [electron-27-code.log](https://github.com/electron/electron/files/12770148/electron-27-code.log)
- Only `Tasks` Output pane is available, and all extensions appear not working
  - This _may_ be due to the aforementioned `npm` errors
- ~~**Menu bars appear with black foreground text color + white background**~~
  - It turns out this was due to `--force-dark-mode` not being passed properly by my modified `code` wrapper script (was missing `~/.config/electron27.flags` file)
  - Other than this, the menu appears similar to the `native` placement & behavior, but no crash on startup!

[1]: https://<redacted-host>/packages/electron27-bin

I have struggled to reproduce this in a self-contained environment, but after spending a few minutes on it the other day, I somehow have ended up with something that causes `code --user-data-dir=$(mktemp -d)` (VSCode 1.85.1, which uses Electron 25.9.7) to crash before it ever shows me a window, *most of the time*.

It's not perfect, but being able to do it with zero setup, repeatedly, means I can easily generate a dozen crashes in a row, whereas before, I only knew how to cause a crash with my own non-trivial `~/.config/Code` data dir.
(Now I suspect the only problem with my existing VSCode state is that it has maximized windows, themselves the problem)

---

While I could sometimes repro after spamming the "new window" keybind and mouse clicking (i.e. the double-click to maximize a window) for a while, KWin automation was way more effective. In `~/.config/kwinrulesrc` I now have:
```ini
[2fd1b564-27d0-46f6-ae06-64a0470c8884]
Description=VSCode/Electron Wayland crash reproducer
maximizehoriz=true
maximizehorizrule=3
maximizevert=true
maximizevertrule=3
minimize=true
minimizerule=3
wmclass=code|electron
wmclasscomplete=true
wmclassmatch=3
```

And this is what it looks like in the UI (which is how I configured it, sadly I see no export/import):
![image](https://github.com/electron/electron/assets/77424/e1136ddb-017e-4f42-9a91-77f78d0b86e2)

---

With that in place, I was able to reproduce startup crashes in Electron 26 apps as well.
I'm on NixOS, so that gave me a relatively easy (if perhaps ridiculous-looking) way to try that:
```sh
env $(nix-build -E 'with import<nixpkgs>{}; pocket-casts.override { electron = electron_26; }' --no-out-link)/bin/pocket-casts \
    --ozone-platform-hint=auto --enable-features=WaylandWindowDecorations --user-data-dir=$(mktemp -d)
```
The `electron` binary from the `electron_26` package itself crashed at least once, and both that and the `pocket-cast`-with-`electron_26` were able to cause some spooky crashes *in other processes* (ignoring the weird GPU interactions, it looks like `kwin_wayland` crashed twice in `QtWaylandServer::xdg_toplevel::handle_set_title` calling `KWin::Window::findWindowWithSameCaption` which then iterates over windows - maybe that one is just a bad Wayland window state that kwin doesn't handle correctly, hard to tell really).

One unmistakeable sign it was about to crash on startup, btw, was seeing the (minimized) window *in more than one taskbar* (I have per-monitor taskbars set to filter only to windows on that monitor, so the Electron window must be in a weird state for it to show up on multiple monitors' taskbars like that).

---

However, repeating the same experiments with Electron 27 produced no crashes on startup (in line with e.g. https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/39449#issuecomment-1741330933).
I've also tried VSCode Insiders (2023-12-20 build, which uses Electron 27.1.3), and I similarly couldn't reproduce a startup crash, so if it still exists, it needs conditions I'm not accounting for (or is harder to hit).

~~Sadly, the exit/window close crashes are still there, but they'd be less disurptive to my VSCode experience than not being able to start it at all (without forcing XWayland and passing `--disable-gpu`).~~

After more experimentation, VSCode Insiders doesn't even crash when closing a window (with both `native` and `custom` titlebars, even), there is a different crash when closing the whole app, not sure if related?

---

And of course, since auto-maximizing works to reproduce the bug, what about the opposite?
Yupp, I can finally start my (non-Insiders) VSCode again on Wayland, with GPU acceleration, perfect crisp per-monitor fractional scaling (like I've been waiting for, for months), and even close/open windows, with no crashes, "just" by setting the "Maximized horizontally/vertically" states to "Force" and "No".

It's definitely *weird* to use, you can't even *attempt* to maximize or edge-snap the windows, they feel very "floaty". Fullscreening still seems to work though, so that's a nice potential workaround.

My only regret is that I hadn't picked up on the maximization connection sooner, and tried harder to repro the crash with a fresh `--user-data-dir` (instead of going with XWayland + `--disable-gpu` for months).

**EDIT**: the workaround also appears to fix Obsidian (the other app I use, still stuck on Electron 25).
